title: Any Lifestyle You Want, As Long as It's Not Normal
author: Aaron Renn
summary: Modern media celebrate every lifestyle except normal family arrangements. New York magazine publishes profiles of women regretting motherhood, single mothers by choice, and polyamorous co-parenting—all positioned as valid life strategies. Yet media rarely feature the traditional married nuclear family or normalize conventional relationships. This media pattern signals cultural messaging that departing from established norms is creative while staying within them signals conformity and unfreedom.
points: Media systematically underrepresents traditional married nuclear families
Cultural messaging treats unconventional choices as progressive; conventional as repressive
Major publications feature regretful mothers, solo-by-choice, polyamory as equally valid paths
Framing implies normal families = oppression; alternative arrangements = liberation
Reflects and reinforces declining appeal of traditional family formation
quotes: I always like to say that the media love to rep every lifestyle choice except normal.
